one_liner: Days in the season window when the daily highest temperature was above a heat limit that a paper reports for one crop stage; the limit is for that stage, the window is ours.
Days in the season window when the daily lowest temperature stayed above a hot-night limit reported for a crop stage; the limit is for that stage, the window is ours.
Days in the season window when the daily lowest temperature fell below a cold limit reported for a crop stage; the limit is for that stage, the window is ours.
Days with 20 mm of rain or more (standard ETCCDI index R20mm, not a Bangladesh-specific limit).

Days with rain at or above the BMD heavy-rain limit (a cited row, from a news report of the BMD scale). IMERG is a cell mean, not point rainfall, so it may undercount point extremes. Shown beside R20mm, which uses a lower, standard limit.
The heaviest single day of rain in the season window (ETCCDI Rx1day, here per season window rather than per month; not a Bangladesh-specific limit).
The longest run of days in a row with less than 1 mm of rain (ETCCDI CDD, counted inside the season window).
How much water the air could pull from a well-watered grass surface over the season window (FAO-56 reference evaporation).
Season rain minus season reference evaporation: a simple climate balance, not the Kc-weighted crop balance (that is the crop water use in W4).
How wet the root zone was this season compared with the same season in the other years (z-score; context, only about ten usable SMAP years, so always check n).
How green the land was compared with other years (MODIS NDVI z-score). Its status and years present come from the data status table; only some years are downloaded.
Trend of regional water storage (GRACE-FO, about 300 km effective, shared by neighbouring districts; not district groundwater).
How our evaporation estimate compares with ECOSTRESS satellite evaporation on the demo fields. Not assessed: the ECOSTRESS evaporation units are unresolved.
Whether season rain (NASA IMERG) shows a steady change, a level shift, or neither.
Whether season mean temperature (NASA POWER) shows a steady change, a level shift, or neither.
Whether season reference evaporation shows a steady change, a level shift, or neither.
